clue.text: Spooner's illustrating safe roadside feature

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words that follow

parts.note: marking can mean illustrating or showing, as in marking an occasion
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A remark about a roadside fixture that shows off a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of MARKING PETER gives PARKING METER. Peter is thieves' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated parking device stands by the kerb, so it is a fixture at the side of a street.

clue.text: Seeker of retribution's victorious day in Gaul, it's said

annotationWithheld.why: Seeker of retribution's victorious day in Gaul, it's said (7): no parse found for the homophone of 'victorious day in Gaul' that gives AVENGER
annotationWithheld.clue: Seeker of retribution's victorious day in Gaul, it's said

clue.text: African capital where king hurt Mao in revolution

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in revolution means the letters of the words hurt and Mao are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A political tale of a city where a monarch wounded the Chinese leader during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges HURTMAO to HARTOUM, which follows K.
explanation.definitionFit: Khartoum is the capital city of Sudan, in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Uncovered elbow no good

indicators.note: no here asks for the letter for good to be dropped from the word

parts.note: to elbow someone is to nudge them

explanation.surface: Someone's bare arm joint is declared worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes G out of NUDGE to leave NUDE. 'Elbow' looks like a noun but works as a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked and uncovered are synonyms, both meaning without clothing.

clue.text: Parent has personal problem? Massive rot!

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
BO, body odour, is a classic personal hygiene problem
jumbo means huge or massive

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that a mother has a hygiene issue and that the whole thing is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is body odour, the classic hygiene complaint. The exclamation mark keeps the surface's outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless jargon or gibberish is nonsense, a great deal of rubbish.

clue.text: Article concerned with a sympathetic word

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A grammar note about an article concerning a word of comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense is the soothing 'there, there' said to someone upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a comforting murmur to someone upset, it is a word of consolation.

clue.text: Becomes sleepy again? Goes to bed

definitions.meaning: the question mark flags the pun
to turn in for the night, to withdraw to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going off to sleep; split, the word also reads as tiring once more.

clue.text: Scots, for example, to invest in European currency? That's spooky!

indicators.note: to invest in here means one piece is put inside the other, like money placed in a fund

parts.note: the schilling was the currency of Austria before the euro
the Scots pine is a kind of pine tree

explanation.surface: A wry question about Scottish people putting money into a European currency, followed by a cry that it is eerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' looks like people but is the Scots pine. The Austrian currency before the euro is spelt with SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Spine-chilling describes something frightening enough to send a shiver down the back, which is what spooky things do.

clue.text: Considerate person sup plies a man embracing woman

parts.note: the word supplies, split across a line in the newspaper print, means goods

indicators.note: embracing means one word holds the other within its arms

parts.note: taken as the word man
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A kind person provides for a man who is hugging a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The print splits 'supplies' across a line break; read it as one word. 'embracing' splits the man after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the parable of the helpful traveller in Luke's gospel, so it names anyone who kindly aids a stranger.

clue.text: Knackered bipedal horse

indicators.note: knackered means worn out or broken, so the following word is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausted horse that walks on two legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knackered' rearranges the letters of BIPEDAL. It also means tired in British slang, which suits the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with irregular black and white patches.

clue.text: Virtuoso alternative to Tchaikovsky's First to join backing

indicators.note: backing means the whole string built so far is read from end to start

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: First picks out the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: a seam is a join between two pieces of material

explanation.surface: A musical virtuoso proposed as a replacement for Tchaikovsky's First Concerto, joining the accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the whole string ORTSEAM, not just the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician or master of an art, so a virtuoso.

clue.text: Approaching time, lam, perhaps

parts.note: nigh means near or approaching

explanation.surface: A note that a certain hour is drawing close.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'lam' is the hour 1am. The definition is by example, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: One in the morning is an hour that falls in the dark part of the day, an example of it.

clue.text: Was courageous accepting rejection of self as shabby

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the other into itself

parts.note: dared means showed courage, past tense like was courageous

indicators.note: rejection of means the word for self is turned back the other way

parts.note: the ego is the self

explanation.surface: Someone bravely accepted a rebuff to their pride and was left looking worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns the self round, and 'accepting' places it after the first letter. 'Was courageous' is a past tense, so the synonym is past tense too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has its page corners folded and worn, so it looks tatty and shabby.

clue.text: Rations distributed, about a couple of handfuls, as booming

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the next piece
distributed means the food rations are dealt out and spread into a new arrangement

parts.note: a handful is five, as on one hand, so two of them make ten

explanation.surface: Food is handed out, roughly two handfuls each, amid loud announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' makes STORIAN, which 'about' splits after the S. A handful is five, as on a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentorian voice is very loud, after Stentor, the Greek herald, so booming is a synonym.

clue.text: Roundabout sees ninety-nine turning right, so I cut out going round bend

indicators.note: turning means the Roman number is flipped back to front

parts.note: IC is ninety-nine in Roman numerals, a hundred less one

indicators.note: going round means the scrambled letters surround the piece for the bend
out means the following words are thrown out of order

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend shaped like that letter, as in plumbing

explanation.surface: A driver at a roundabout takes a right turn at speed and cuts across a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes the anagram CUITOS, which 'going round' wraps round the U. 'Roundabout' looks like a road junction but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect and roundabout both describe a route that does not go straight to its end point.

clue.text: In the Americas? I admit it's not!

definitions.text: In the Americas? I admit it's not!

indicators.note: In means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place is in the New World and concedes that it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden across 'AmericAS I Admit'. The whole clue is also the definition: this continent is not in the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent lies east of Europe, far from the New World, so it is a place not in the Americas.

clue.text: Enjoy being embraced by French father with English upbringing

indicators.note: being embraced by means the word for enjoy is held inside the next one

parts.note: pere is French for father
to dig something is slang for enjoying it

explanation.surface: A child enjoys being hugged by a French dad who has an English background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being embraced by' gives PEDIGRE before the E for English. 'dig' meaning enjoy is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree is a person's lineage or background, the line of descent they were raised in.

clue.text: Dubious moment, leader having been ousted

indicators.note: leader having been ousted means the first letter of the word for moment is thrown out

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A shaky period in which a leader was deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader having been ousted' takes J off the front of JIFFY. 'leader' suggests politics but only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or questionable, so it means dubious.

clue.text: More extravagant fire can spread

indicators.note: spread, as a fire spreads, means the letters of the two words scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a fire is capable of spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges FIRECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancier is the comparative of fancy, which means elaborate or showy, so more extravagant.

clue.text: A bit insane, mad, when out to lunch, perhaps?

indicators.note: mad means the preceding words are crazily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is described as slightly crazy, mad, or not all there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ABITINSANE. 'Out to lunch' is slang for crazy, which fits the surface, but here it is literal: away from the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means while not present, and someone out for lunch is away from their desk.

clue.text: Lottery involving male cricketer reported

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, such as a tomcat

indicators.note: reported means we need a word that sounds like the cricketer's role, not its spelling

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball

explanation.surface: A raffle that features a male cricketer, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLA sounds like BOWLER, the cricketer who delivers the ball. A tombola is a raffle common at British fetes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle in which tickets are drawn from a spinning drum, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: Not much of a chance to look at thongs, unfortunately

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: unfortunately means the skimpy underwear word is badly mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has little opportunity to see skimpy underwear, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' makes NGSHOT. 'lo', as in 'lo and behold', is an old call to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a bet or attempt with only a slim prospect of success.

clue.text: Suddenly attack choice of routes?

parts.note: St is an abbreviated street, one kind of route
or offers a choice between two things
M is the motorway prefix in Britain, as in the M1, another kind of route

explanation.surface: A soldier must charge suddenly, choosing between several roads.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'choice of routes' as 'St or M': a street or a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to assault it with a sudden, violent rush.

clue.text: A doctor injected into two feet

indicators.note: injected into means one piece is pushed inside another, like a needle

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor gives an injection into a pair of feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' are metrical feet in poetry, not body parts; the answer is the plural of iambus.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one short then one long syllable, and these are its plural.

clue.text: Colour brings no success to wine at vineyard

indicators.note: brings no means the word for success is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a win is a success
cru is a French term for a vineyard or its classified growth

explanation.surface: A wine merchant notes that a colour does nothing for a wine's chances at the vineyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings no' takes WIN out of 'wine', leaving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade, the colour of unbleached linen.

clue.text: African capital or two following name for another, but no capital

indicators.note: following means the word for two comes after the rest
but no capital means the initial capital letter of that city is dropped

parts.note: another African capital, Cairo, the capital of Egypt
bi is the prefix meaning two, as in bicycle

explanation.surface: A puzzling definition of one capital in terms of another that is no capital at all.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRO is CAIRO without its capital letter C. 'or' is a link. 'another' only works because 'African capital' is in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Spanish city firm with incompetent board

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: incompetent means the following word is botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A company in Spain is run by an inept board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incompetent' makes RDOBA. Cordoba is in Andalusia, southern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordoba is a historic city in Andalusia, southern Spain.

clue.text: I, for instance, shift normal manure

indicators.note: shift means the letters of the following two words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener talks about moving an ordinary load of dung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' rearranges NORMALMANURE. 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I stands for one in the Latin numbering system, so it is an example.
